method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP) 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease' (published 21 April 2026), 20 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC13288312). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from ERA Working Group on Inherited Kidney Disorders, ERKNet and PKD International (Müller RU, Messchendorp AL, Birn H, et al.), Nephrology Dialysis Transplantation 37(5):825-839 (doi 10.1093/ndt/gfab312) 'An update on the use of tolvaptan for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: consensus statement on behalf of the ERA Working Group on Inherited Kidney Disorders, the European Rare Kidney Disease Reference Network and Polycystic Kidney Disease International' (published online 19 November 2021), 9 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC9035348). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 adds S2, the ERA/ERKNet/PKD International tolvaptan consensus update (Europe PMC JATS XML, tables stripped), paraphrased and hash-anchored; it is the ERA algorithm S1 refers to. The S1 claims and anchors are unchanged from edition 1.0.

claims.claim: **Diagnose clinically or genetically.** Screen at-risk adults with ultrasound; use CT or MRI when the result is unclear or for prognosis. Counsel people before screening about what it may show.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Genomic testing is publicly funded in Australia** (MBS item 74 301, for suspected monogenic cystic kidney disease) but only a nephrologist or clinical geneticist can request it, and genetic counselling comes first. New Zealand has no public subsidy.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A negative genetic test does not exclude a genetic cause:** PKD1 pseudogenes and exome-based panels can miss the variant. If suspicion stays high, consider further testing such as whole-genome sequencing.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Blood pressure follows the KDIGO 2021 BP-in-CKD guideline**, though the ADPKD targets differ. Home BP monitoring is a practical substitute for ambulatory monitoring, notably by telehealth in rural and remote areas.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Chronic kidney pain (over 3 months):** first rule out other causes and acute events such as cyst rupture. Step up from paracetamol and heat, to TENS or acupuncture, to spinal cord stimulation, to nephrectomy; refractory pain needs a multidisciplinary team.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Look for UTI when there is fever, flank or acute abdominal pain, a raised white count or raised CRP.** Australian guidance gives nitrofurantoin for 5 days, but not in CKD G3–G5. Infected kidney cysts need a lipid-soluble antibiotic given for longer.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Standard CKD care applies, with two exceptions:** SGLT2 inhibitors are not advised for now, and HIF-PHIs are not recommended for anaemia, because trials excluded people with ADPKD.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transplant is the preferred kidney replacement therapy.** Living donation gives better outcomes, but related donors need genetic testing, which may limit who can donate.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat polycystic liver disease by symptoms and severity;** do not over-treat people without symptoms. Somatostatin analogues suit a markedly enlarged liver with severe symptoms but are not publicly funded here. Counsel on hormone effects (including contraception) on liver volume.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not screen everyone for intracranial aneurysm.** Screen (time-of-flight MRA without gadolinium, or CT angiography) with a family history of aneurysm or subarachnoid haemorrhage, a high-risk job such as pilot, major surgery, or marked anxiety. Keep known unruptured aneurysms under surveillance.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **KDIGO: start tolvaptan in adults with eGFR ≥ 25 mL/min/1.73m2 who are at risk of rapid progression** (Mayo class 1C–1E, or eGFR falling by ≥3 mL/min per 1.73 m2 a year). CARI endorses this plus the more detailed ERA-EDTA algorithm for identifying rapid progressors for subsidy.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use shared decision-making, especially over age 55,** where there is no trial evidence. Start at the lowest split dose and titrate under physician supervision with nephrologist input.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Liver injury is a serious risk: test LFTs monthly for 18 months, then quarterly.** Expect thirst, polyuria and nocturia; make sure fluid intake is enough, especially in hot weather.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No other drug is recommended to slow ADPKD:** not mTOR inhibitors, statins, somatostatin analogues, metformin or complementary medicines, because the evidence is insufficient.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **ERA: tolvaptan can be started in adults aged 55 or under with eGFR of at least 25 mL/min/1.73 m2 who have, or are likely to have, rapidly progressive disease,** judged with a stepwise algorithm. Do not start it when eGFR is high for age: at 40–44 years, 90 or above; 45–49 years, 75 or above; 50–55 years, 60 or above (no eGFR limit under 40).
claims.locator: ERA Working Group on Inherited Kidney Disorders, ERKNet and PKD International (Müller RU, Messchendorp AL, Birn H, et al.), Nephrology Dialysis Transplantation 37(5):825-839 (doi 10.1093/ndt/gfab312), 'An update on the use of tolvaptan for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: consensus statement on behalf of the ERA Working Group on Inherited Kidney Disorders, the European Rare Kidney Disease Reference Network and Polycystic Kidney Disease International', published online 19 November 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9035348/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Why ERA uses 55:** a REPRISE subgroup showed no benefit over 55, and most rapid progressors reach kidney failure before then (average age at kidney replacement 58). The limit is not absolute. ERA does not advise starting before 18, and suggests stopping as kidney failure nears (for example eGFR below 15).
claims.locator: ERA Working Group on Inherited Kidney Disorders, ERKNet and PKD International (Müller RU, Messchendorp AL, Birn H, et al.), Nephrology Dialysis Transplantation 37(5):825-839 (doi 10.1093/ndt/gfab312), 'An update on the use of tolvaptan for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: consensus statement on behalf of the ERA Working Group on Inherited Kidney Disorders, the European Rare Kidney Disease Reference Network and Polycystic Kidney Disease International', published online 19 November 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9035348/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Proving rapid progression (ERA):** a confirmed eGFR fall of 3 mL/min/1.73 m2 or more a year, based on at least five creatinine values over 4 years or more (CKD-EPI equation), with other causes excluded, especially with non-linear decline, older age or several comorbidities.
claims.locator: ERA Working Group on Inherited Kidney Disorders, ERKNet and PKD International (Müller RU, Messchendorp AL, Birn H, et al.), Nephrology Dialysis Transplantation 37(5):825-839 (doi 10.1093/ndt/gfab312), 'An update on the use of tolvaptan for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: consensus statement on behalf of the ERA Working Group on Inherited Kidney Disorders, the European Rare Kidney Disease Reference Network and Polycystic Kidney Disease International', published online 19 November 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9035348/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Predicting it (ERA): use the Mayo imaging class as the main tool,** with scans read by radiologists or nephrologists experienced in ADPKD. Classes 1D and 1E mean rapid progression. Class 1C overlaps with slow disease, so look for more evidence (a PROPKD score above 6, a truncating PKD1 variant, early hypertension or urological symptoms, or dialysis before 60 in two or more first-degree relatives). Atypical kidneys or classes 1A and 1B make rapid progression unlikely.
claims.locator: ERA Working Group on Inherited Kidney Disorders, ERKNet and PKD International (Müller RU, Messchendorp AL, Birn H, et al.), Nephrology Dialysis Transplantation 37(5):825-839 (doi 10.1093/ndt/gfab312), 'An update on the use of tolvaptan for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: consensus statement on behalf of the ERA Working Group on Inherited Kidney Disorders, the European Rare Kidney Disease Reference Network and Polycystic Kidney Disease International', published online 19 November 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9035348/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Reconsider tolvaptan when something else could explain the eGFR loss:** proteinuria of 1 g/day or more, vascular disease such as coronary disease or stroke, uncontrolled severe hypertension, or diabetes. Gather more information, including MRI or CT if not yet done, to confirm ADPKD is the main cause.
claims.locator: ERA Working Group on Inherited Kidney Disorders, ERKNet and PKD International (Müller RU, Messchendorp AL, Birn H, et al.), Nephrology Dialysis Transplantation 37(5):825-839 (doi 10.1093/ndt/gfab312), 'An update on the use of tolvaptan for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: consensus statement on behalf of the ERA Working Group on Inherited Kidney Disorders, the European Rare Kidney Disease Reference Network and Polycystic Kidney Disease International', published online 19 November 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9035348/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Dosing:** start with 45 mg on waking and 15 mg 8 hours later, then titrate straight away, weekly or monthly, towards 90/30 mg a day unless it is not tolerated or drug interactions (CYP3A inhibitors or inducers) prevent it; benefit was proven only when aiming for 90/30 mg. Do not dose by urine osmolality, though it can help check adherence.
claims.locator: ERA Working Group on Inherited Kidney Disorders, ERKNet and PKD International (Müller RU, Messchendorp AL, Birn H, et al.), Nephrology Dialysis Transplantation 37(5):825-839 (doi 10.1093/ndt/gfab312), 'An update on the use of tolvaptan for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: consensus statement on behalf of the ERA Working Group on Inherited Kidney Disorders, the European Rare Kidney Disease Reference Network and Polycystic Kidney Disease International', published online 19 November 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9035348/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Liver and other checks:** transaminases rise above three times normal in about 5% of patients, usually reversibly once the drug stops. Do not re-expose someone after significant liver toxicity, and rule out other causes. Check sodium, creatinine or urea and body weight regularly.
claims.locator: ERA Working Group on Inherited Kidney Disorders, ERKNet and PKD International (Müller RU, Messchendorp AL, Birn H, et al.), Nephrology Dialysis Transplantation 37(5):825-839 (doi 10.1093/ndt/gfab312), 'An update on the use of tolvaptan for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: consensus statement on behalf of the ERA Working Group on Inherited Kidney Disorders, the European Rare Kidney Disease Reference Network and Polycystic Kidney Disease International', published online 19 November 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9035348/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Polyuria is expected in almost everyone:** urine output averages 5–8 L a day, which often means hourly daytime voiding and two to three times a night, most marked at higher GFR. Suggest less dietary sodium, starting on a weekend and not taking the second dose too late; pause tolvaptan whenever dehydration threatens (diarrhoea, vomiting, no access to water).
claims.locator: ERA Working Group on Inherited Kidney Disorders, ERKNet and PKD International (Müller RU, Messchendorp AL, Birn H, et al.), Nephrology Dialysis Transplantation 37(5):825-839 (doi 10.1093/ndt/gfab312), 'An update on the use of tolvaptan for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: consensus statement on behalf of the ERA Working Group on Inherited Kidney Disorders, the European Rare Kidney Disease Reference Network and Polycystic Kidney Disease International', published online 19 November 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9035348/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Keep sodium under 2 g a day (87 mmol) and protein at 0.8 g/kg** to reduce urine output modestly, particularly on tolvaptan. Refer to a kidney-specialised dietitian. Special diets, including ketogenic diets, have no evidence.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Drink 2–3 L/day, mainly water, if eGFR ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m2,** adjusted for the person and climate. Moderate caffeine (<400 mg per day) is fine.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **ERA, for people not on tolvaptan:** extra water is not an equal substitute for the drug, but it seems prudent to advise a low-salt diet (3–5 g a day) and a high water intake (3–4 L a day).
claims.locator: ERA Working Group on Inherited Kidney Disorders, ERKNet and PKD International (Müller RU, Messchendorp AL, Birn H, et al.), Nephrology Dialysis Transplantation 37(5):825-839 (doi 10.1093/ndt/gfab312), 'An update on the use of tolvaptan for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: consensus statement on behalf of the ERA Working Group on Inherited Kidney Disorders, the European Rare Kidney Disease Reference Network and Polycystic Kidney Disease International', published online 19 November 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9035348/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Obesity is linked to faster progression.** Refer for weight management (with care to avoid malnutrition in CKD G4–G5) and encourage more than 150 min/week of exercise plus 1 h of strength training.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pregnancy is not contraindicated,** but risk rises with reduced kidney function, uncontrolled hypertension or past pre-eclampsia. Offer pre-pregnancy counselling and multidisciplinary care. ⚠️ **Stop tolvaptan before conception** (teratogenic).
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In pregnancy, target BP ≤130/85 mmHg** (<135/85 mmHg with pre-existing hypertension), and give low-dose aspirin 75–150 mg/day, ideally in the evening, from week 12 to 36.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not screen children without symptoms by ultrasound.** Test only when indicated (for example hypertension or haematuria) under a paediatric nephrologist; check BP in every child with or at risk of ADPKD.
claims.locator: CARI Guidelines, Internal Medicine Journal (RACP), 'Caring for Australians and New ZealandeRs with kidney Impairment guideline commentary on kidney disease: improving global outcomes 2025 guidelines for diagnosis and management of autosomal polycystic kidney disease', published 21 April 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13288312, retrieved 2026-09-23
